lineage_context.teaching_goal: Use Vallisneria americana to teach a submerged basal-ribbon aquatic with inferior ovary and highly specialized water-surface pollination.

project_scope.note: The project pool has one Hydrocharitaceae concept. Family recognition is built around Vallisneria's strap-leaf rosette, dioecious flowers and surface-pollination mechanics. Distribution disagreements between modern Kew and FNA are left for species-range reconciliation.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start underwater: Vallisneria grows as a rooted stoloniferous rosette of long strap-like leaves with no elongate leafy stem. Then look for reproductive structures at the water surface.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Submerged perennial with basal linear ribbon-like leaves. In Vallisneria the blade shows rows of large air spaces beside the midvein, often creating a three-zoned appearance.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Hydrocharitaceae generally has epigynous flowers with an inferior ovary and flowers subtended by a spathe. Vallisneria is dioecious: tiny male flowers detach and float to the surface, while female flowers are raised to the surface on a long slender peduncle.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Elongate cylindrical fruit developing from the inferior ovary; after fertilization the female peduncle coils helically and retracts the developing fruit underwater.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Basal submerged ribbon leaves + no leafy stem + floating free male flowers + female flower on a long coiling peduncle is the Vallisneria package.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: submerged rosette → leaf lacunae → male/female surface pollination → inferior ovary → coiling peduncle → comparison anchors
visual_lesson.intro: Vallisneria is an ideal visual aquatic lesson because the plant looks simple until reproduction starts: male flowers break loose and float, while a female flower rides a long stalk to the surface and is reeled back underwater after fertilization.

steps.title: 1 · Start with the underwater ribbon rosette
steps.look_for: Long basal linear leaves arising from a short rooted axis and spreading from stolons, without an elongate leafy stem.
steps.why_it_matters: Separates Vallisneria from stem-forming pondweeds before flowering.

steps.title: 2 · Look for the three-zone leaf anatomy
steps.look_for: Rows of lacunae on each side of the midvein producing a lighter central zone flanked by darker zones.
steps.why_it_matters: A high-value FNA vegetative character for Vallisneria.

steps.title: 3 · Male flowers break free
steps.look_for: Many tiny staminate flower buds enclosed underwater, then individual male flowers released to float at the surface.
steps.why_it_matters: One half of the family's memorable surface-pollination mechanism.

steps.title: 4 · Female flower rides to the surface
steps.look_for: A solitary pistillate flower held at the water surface by a very long slender peduncle.
steps.why_it_matters: Makes the separate male/female strategy visually obvious.

steps.title: 5 · Confirm the inferior ovary and coiling peduncle
steps.look_for: Long inferior ovary below the flower; after fertilization the peduncle coils helically and draws the developing fruit underwater.
steps.why_it_matters: Links family-level inferior-ovary anatomy to a unique field behavior.

comparisons.title: Hydrocharitaceae vs Alismataceae
comparisons.rule: Both can form basal aquatic rosettes. Sagittaria/Alismataceae usually sends an emergent flower stalk with conspicuous 3-petaled flowers and many achenes; Vallisneria stays ribbon-leaved underwater and uses free-floating male flowers plus a female surface flower on a long coiling peduncle.

comparisons.title: Hydrocharitaceae vs Potamogetonaceae
comparisons.rule: Potamogeton has elongate leafy stems, axillary stipules/prophylls and an emergent dense flower spike. Vallisneria has a basal ribbon rosette, no leafy elongate stem, dioecious flowers and an inferior ovary.

comparisons.title: Hydrocharitaceae vs aquatic Araceae
comparisons.rule: Pistia and duckweed Araceae float at the surface and are recognized by rosette/frond plus spathe-spadix lineage characters; Vallisneria is rooted and submerged with strap leaves and specialized surface pollination.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not settle Texas/Hays nativity from the family module. FNA includes Texas for Vallisneria americana, while the current Kew distribution listing is narrower; species-range reconciliation should handle that conflict explicitly.

genera.fast_cue: submerged basal strap leaves + free-floating male flowers + female surface flower on long coiling peduncle

taxonomy_reconciliation.note: Accepted current species. FNA and current Kew differ in displayed distribution treatment; leave Texas/Hays range resolution to the species workflow.
Current Kew treats the varietal name as a synonym of V. americana.
